questions.q: A nucleus <math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>,</mo></math> with a finite de-broglie wavelength <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">λ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo></math> undergoes spontaneous fission into two nuclei <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> of equal mass. <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> flies in the same direction as that of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>,</mo></math> while <math><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> flies in the opposite direction with a velocity equal to half of that of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The de-Broglie wavelengths <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">λ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow></msub><mi> </mi></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">λ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></msub></math> of B and C are respectively:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
hλA=hλB-hλC …(i)
Also λC=2λB ...(ii)
From equation (i) & (ii),
1λA=1λB-12λB
λB=λA2; λC=λA

questions.q:
In photoelectric effect an em-wave is incident on a metal surface and electrons are ejected from the surface. If the work function of the metal is 2.14 eV and stopping potential is 2 V , what is the wavelength of the em-wave ?
(Given hc $=1242 \mathrm{eVnm}$ where h is the Planck's constant and c is the speed of light in vaccum.)
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q:
The threshold wavelength for photoelectric emission from a material is 5500 A∘. Photoelectrons will be emitted, when this material is illuminated with monochromatic radiation from a

A. 75 W infra-red lamp

B. 10 W infra-red lamp

C. 75 W ultra-violet lamp

D. 10 W ultra-violet lamp

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, threshold wavelength λth=5500 Å=550 nm

For photoelectric emission, the wavelength of the light should be less than 550 nm.

Wavelength of infrared radiation extends from 700 nm-1 mm and that of ultraviolet radiation is 100-400 nm.

Since, UV light has less wavelength than 550 nm, so only UV would be able to emit photoelectrons.

questions.q: What should be the order of arrangement of de-Broglie wavelength of electron <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></msub></mfenced></math>, an <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math>-particle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">α</mi></msub></mfenced></math> and proton <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi></msub></mfenced></math> given that all have the same kinetic energy ?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
λ=hp=h2mE∝1m

mα>mp>me

so λe>λp>λα

questions.q: For the photoelectric effect, the maximum kinetic energy Ek of the photoelectrons is plotted against the frequency (v) of the incident photons as shown in figure. The slope of the graph gives
options: Ratio of Planck’s constant to electric charge
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Comparing Einstein's equation Kmax=hv-hv0, with y=mx+c, we get slope, m=h, which is Planck’s constant.

questions.q: The de Broglie wavelengths for an electron and a photon are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math> respectively. For the same kinetic energy of electron and photon, which of the following presents the correct relation between the de Broglie wavelengths of two?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
De-Broglie wavelength for electron is given by, λe=h2mk

For photon k=hcλp⇒λp=hck. Therefore,

λe=hλp2mhc

λp∝λe2

questions.q: In a photoelectric experiment, increasing the intensity of incident light:
options: increases the number of photons incident and also increases the K.E. of the ejected electrons.
increases the frequency of photons incident and increases the K.E. of the ejected electrons.
increases the number of photons incident and the K.E. of the ejected electrons remains unchanged.
increases the frequency of photons incident and the K.E. of the ejected electrons remains unchanged.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: The relation between the energy of photons and the intensity of photons is, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>I</mi><mi>A</mi></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> is the number of photons, if we increase the number of photons then frequency does not change it means total energy and kinetic energy of photon remains unchanged but due to to this property the intensity of light is increased.

questions.q: When photon of energy <math><mn>4.0</mn><mi></mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> strikes the surface of a metal <math><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo></math> the ejected photoelectrons have maximum kinetic energy <math><msub><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> and de-Broglie wavelength <math><msub><mrow><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><mo>.</mo></math> The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons liberated from another metal <math><mi>B</mi></math> by photon of energy <math><mn>4.50</mn><mi></mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> is <math><msub><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><mo>-</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow></mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mo>.</mo></math> If the de-Broglie wavelength of these photoelectrons <math><msub><mrow><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mrow><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo></math> then the work function of metal <math><mi>B</mi></math> is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Relation between de-Broglie wavelength and K.E. is
λ=h2(KE)me⇒λ∝1KE
λAλB=KEBKEA
⇒12=TA-1.5TA⇒TA=2 eV
∴KEB=2-1.5=0.5 eV
ϕB=4.5-0.5=4 eV

questions.q: A parallel beam of light of wavelength <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>900</mn><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></math> and intensity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><msup><mi>Wm</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> is incident on a surface perpendicular to the beam. The number of photons crossing <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math> area perpendicular to the beam in one second is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Wavelength of incident beam λ=900×10-9 m

Energy of a single photon E=hcλ.

Intensity is defined as power per unit area. Therefore,

Intensity of incident beam I=EtA

If the number of photons crossing the given area per second is n, then

n=Enet Esingle pholon =IAλhc

⇒n=1001×10-4900×10-96.62×10-34×3×108=4.5×1016.

questions.q:
If the deBroglie wavelength of an electron is equal to $10^{-}$ times the wavelength of a photon of frequency $6 \times 10^{14}\mathrm{Hz}$, then the speed of electron is equal to :

(Speed of light $\left.=3 \times 10^{8} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\right)$

Planck's constant $=6.63 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{~J} . \mathrm{s}$

Mass of electron $\left.=9.1 \times 10^{-31} \mathrm{~kg}\right)$
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: Average force exerted on a non-reflecting surface at normal incidence is $2.4 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~N}$. If $360 \mathrm{~W} / \mathrm{cm}^2$ is the light energy flux during span of 1 hour 30 minutes, Then the area of the surface is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Pressure }=\frac{I}{C}=\frac{F}{A} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{360}{10^{-4} \times 3 \times 10^8}=\frac{2.4 \times 10^{-4}}{A} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{A}=2 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~m}^2=0.02 \mathrm{~m}^2\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A proton and an α-particle are accelerated from rest by 2 V and 4 V potentials, respectively. The ratio of their de-Broglie wavelength is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the de Broglie wavelength of the proton is given by

λp=h2mpqpV   ...1

The formula to calculate the de Broglie wavelength of the alpha particle is given by

λα=h2mαqαV'   ...2

Divide equation (1) by equation (2) and simplify to obtain the required ratio.

λpλα=mαmp×qαV'qpV   ...3

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required ratio.

λpλα=41×2×41×2=4:1

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Two photons having equal linear momenta have equal wavelengths.

Statement II: If the wavelength of the photon is decreased, then the momentum and energy of a photon will also decrease.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> and Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> are false
Both Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> and Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> are true
Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is true but Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> is false
Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is false but Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> is true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If linear momentum are equal then wavelength also equal.

The momentum p and energy E of a photon is given by,

p=hλ, E=hcλ; where c is speed of light and h is Plank's constant.

On decreasing wavelength, momentum and energy of photon increases.

questions.q: Particle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mtext>m</mtext><mtext>A</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mtext>m</mtext><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> moving along the <math><mtext>x</mtext></math> -axis with velocity <math><mrow><msub><mtext>v</mtext><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></math> collides elastically with another particle <math><mtext>B</mtext></math> at rest having mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mtext>m</mtext><mtext>B</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mtext>m</mtext><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math>. If both the particles move along the <math><mtext>x</mtext></math> -axis after the collision, the change <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>∆</mo><mi>λ</mi></math> in the wavelength of the particle <math><mtext>A</mtext></math>, in terms of its de-Broglie wavelength <math><mrow><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></mfenced></mrow></math> before the collision is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
v1=2m/30m2+m3+m2−m3vm2+m3=v5

For particle A,

Initial de-Broglie wavelength

λ0=hm2v=2hmv

Final de-Broglie wavelength after collision.

λ1=hm2v5=10hmv=5λ0

Change in De-Broglie wavelength Δλ=λi−λ0=4λ0

questions.q: Light is incident normally on a completely absorbing surface with an energy flux of <math><mi> </mi><mn>25</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> . If the surface has an area of <math><mi> </mi><mn>25</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> , the momentum transferred to the surface in <math> <mrow> <mtext>40</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>min</mtext></mrow> </math> time duration will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The power of the incident light is P=25  W cm-2×25 cm2
=625 W
Energy incident per second, E=hcλ=625 J
Momentum incident per second, p=Ec=hλ=625c
∴ Total momentum transferred to the surface =625c×40×60
=5×10-3 N s

questions.q: An electron in the ground state of the hydrogen atom has the orbital radius of $5.3 \times 10^{-11} \mathrm{~m}$ while that for the electron in third excited state is $8.48 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{~m}$. The ratio of the de Broglie wavelengths of electron in the excited state to that in the ground state is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\lambda=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{mv}}\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{mvr}=\frac{\mathrm{nh}}{2 \pi} \\
& \mathrm{mv}=\frac{\mathrm{nh}}{2 \pi \mathrm{r}} \\
& \lambda=\frac{2 \pi \mathrm{rh}}{\mathrm{nh}} \\
& \lambda \propto \frac{\mathrm{r}}{\mathrm{n}} \\
& \frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_4}=\frac{\mathrm{r}_1 \mathrm{n}_4}{\mathrm{n}_1 \mathrm{r}_4}=\frac{5.3 \times 10^{-11} \times 4}{1 \times 84.8 \times 10^{-11}} \\
& \frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_4}=\frac{1}{4}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: In an experiment with photoelectric effect, the stopping potential,
options: increases with increase in the intensity of the incident light
decreases with increase in the intensity of the incident light
increases with increase in the wavelength of the incident light
is $\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}}\right)$ times the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From Einstein photoelectric equation
$\frac{h c}{\lambda}=\phi+e V_S$

Maximum K.E. $=(\mathrm{K})_{\max }=e V s$
So, $V_S=\frac{(\mathrm{K})_{\max }}{e}$

questions.q: The ratio of wavelengths of proton and deuteron accelerated by potential <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></math>. Then, the ratio of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></math> will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Kinetic energy gained by a charged particle accelerated by a potential V is qV

KE=qV

Using relation between momentum and kinetic energy

⇒p22 m=qV⇒p=2mqV

We know that momentum of charged particle is p=hλ.

Thus, λ=h2mqV

Now, λpλd=mdVdmpVp

⇒12=2VdVp⇒VpVd=4

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : Stopping potential in photoelectric effect does not depend on the power of the light source.

Statement II : For a given metal, the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectron depends on the wavelength of the incident light.

In the light of above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Both statement I and statement II are correct
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Stopping potential depends on frequency of incident light and nature of the emitter material. It is independent of the power of the light source.

Maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons is stated asKEmax=hν-ϕ=hcλ-ϕ, Where, h is the Planck’s constant, ν is the frequency, λ is wavelength of incident light and ϕ is the work function of the metal surface.

Thus, the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectron depends on the wavelength of the incident light.

So both statements I and II are correct

questions.q: An electron (of mass <math><mi>m</mi></math> ) and a photon have the same energy <math><mi>E</mi></math> in the range of a few <math><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>. The ratio of the de-Broglie wavelength associated with the electron and the wavelength of the photon is ( <math><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mo>=</mo></math> speed of light in vacuum)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
λd for electron =h2mE
λ for photon =hCE
Ratio =h2mEEhC=1CE2m

questions.q:
When UV light of wavelength $300 \mathrm{~nm}$ is incident on the metal surface having work function $2.13 \mathrm{eV}$, electron emission takes place. The stopping potential is:
(Given hc $=1240 \mathrm{eV} \mathrm{nm}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}-\phi=\mathrm{e} . \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{s}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1240}{300} \mathrm{eV}-2.13 \mathrm{eV}=\mathrm{eVs} \\ & \Rightarrow 4.13 \mathrm{eV}-2.13 \mathrm{eV}=\mathrm{eVs} . \\ & \Rightarrow \text { So, } \quad \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{s}}=2 \mathrm{volt}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Proton <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>)</mo></math> and electron <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mo>)</mo></math> will have same de-Broglie wavelength when the ratio of their momentum is (assume, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1849</mn></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></math>)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The De Broglie wavelength is λ=hmv

The momentum is given by p=mv

The momentum of proton is pp=mpvp

The momentum of electron is p'=meve

Since h is the Planck's constant and it is given that both wavelengths are same, i.e.

λp=λe, so pp=p'.

questions.q: In a photoelectric effect experiment a light of frequency <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn></math> times the threshold frequency is made to fall on the surface of photosensitive material. Now if the frequency is halved and intensity is doubled, the number of photo electrons emitted will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, fi=f0. Now, f=fi2=f02.

Since f02<f0 i.e. the incident frequency is less than threshold frequency. Hence, there will be no emission of photoelectrons.

Therefore, current =0 and no photo electrons will be emitted.

questions.q: A particle of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mi>M</mi></math> at rest disintegrates into two particles of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>M</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mi>M</mi></math>, respectively, having non zero velocities. The ratio of de-Broglie wavelength of particle of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>M</mi></math> to that of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mi>M</mi></math> will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
λ=hp

Both the particles will move with momentum same in magnitude and opposite in direction.

So de Broglie wavelength of both will be same, i.e., ratio 1:1.

questions.solution:
P=2 mW
λ=500 nm
Number of photons will be emitted per second is,
n=Phcλ=2×10-3×500×10-96.6×10-34×3×108
=5×1015
